solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Do wait at table (5)

blocks.note: 'do' in the sense of doing time: completing a prison sentence
what a waiter does: bringing food to diners

annotation.surface: An instruction to a new waiter: go and wait on the tables.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction, but 'Do' stands alone as the first definition: to do a prison term is to serve it.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses of one verb: completing a sentence in prison, and bringing dishes to diners.

entries.clue: US uncle stopping to observe plant (6)

indicatorNotes.stopping: the uncle stops up the middle of the other word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: to see = to observe
Uncle Sam personifies the United States

annotation.surface: An American relative blocks someone from watching a factory or a houseplant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory next to the surface's talk of observing, but it is a crop grown for its seeds.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: this is a flowering plant cultivated for its oily seeds.

entries.clue: Arrival (not the first) in car arena, peep curiously (12)

indicatorNotes.curiously: the letters are arranged in a strange, curious way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone takes a curious peek at a stock-car stadium as a driver pulls in.
annotation.walkthrough: '(not the first)' looks like an instruction to drop a first letter, but it is part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: showing up again means arriving for a second or later time.

entries.clue: Room-mate that’s hard to miss and hard to discuss? (8)

annotation.definition: Room-mate that’s hard to miss and hard to discuss?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a person sharing a flat; the setter means something that is 'in the room'

blocks.clueFragment: that’s hard to miss and hard to discuss?
blocks.note: the idiom for an obvious problem everyone avoids mentioning: huge, yet unspoken

annotation.surface: A flatmate so awkward that nobody can ignore them or talk about them.
annotation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'the elephant in the room': a problem too big to miss that no one will raise.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the proverbial beast in the room is enormous and obvious but tactfully unmentioned.

entries.clue: Surrounded by a fog concealing day (6)

indicatorNotes.concealing: the fog hides the day inside itself

blocks.note: kept as is
mist = fog
d = day, the standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Someone is lost in a fog so thick it blots out the daylight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded by' reads as a description of being in the fog, but it is the definition, a preposition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both prepositions mean in the middle of something.

entries.clue: Check part of flower (4)

blocks.note: check in the sense of hold back or stop a flow
the stalk that holds up the bloom

annotation.surface: A gardener is told to inspect a piece of a bloom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as 'inspect', but here it means 'hold back', as in stemming bleeding.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a verb for stopping a flow, and the stalk of a flower.

entries.clue: Liveliness of elf, last to ascend to top (6)

indicatorNotes.last to ascend to top: in a down answer, the final letter climbs up to the first position

blocks.note: a sprite is an elf or fairy; its last letter E moves to the top

annotation.surface: An elf's energy is described as the last one to climb to the summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ascend' works because this is a down clue: moving a letter to the top of the column puts it first.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, borrowed from French: lively wit and spirit.

entries.clue: Never-ending mess, I’ll go wild about it (9)

indicatorNotes.go wild: the letters run riot into a new order
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: MESS + I'LL rearranged, split LIM…LESS
kept as is, placed inside

annotation.surface: Someone vows to fly into a rage over an endless untidy mess.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'I’ll' is ignored, leaving the letters ILL.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: having no limit means having no end.

entries.clue: Excessive spending? New age tax — craven! (12)

indicatorNotes.New: the letters are made new, into a fresh order

blocks.note: anagram indicator
anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: Someone rails against a new levy on the times as lavish and cowardly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New age' looks like one phrase, the spiritual movement, but 'New' is the instruction and only 'age' belongs to the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: lavish, wasteful outlay beyond what is sensible.

entries.clue: Small and almost defenceless reptile (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: the word is not quite complete: its last letter goes

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing sizes
NAKED = defenceless, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A little, nearly helpless lizard or tortoise.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue sounds like a description of a vulnerable creature, but 'reptile' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the legless serpent is one kind of reptile.

entries.clue: Saintly fisherman welcoming church feature and counter for steps (9)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the fisherman takes the church feature inside himself

blocks.note: St Peter was a fisherman before he was an apostle
a dome, as on St Paul's

annotation.surface: A holy fisherman welcomes visitors to his church, pointing out a staircase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steps' suggests the stone steps of a church, but the counter tallies a walker's footsteps.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the gadget worn by walkers tallies each footstep.

entries.clue: Animal you picked up (3)

indicatorNotes.picked up: as a microphone picks up a sound: what is heard, not written

blocks.note: the pronoun, as heard; the spelling wanted is an animal's

annotation.surface: Someone scoops up a pet and is told: you, the animal, lifted it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as lifting the animal, but it means heard: a female sheep sounds exactly like 'you'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a female sheep is an animal.

entries.clue: Shunning pleasure at start, Spartan out to change high flyer? (9)

indicatorNotes.Shunning: the letter is avoided and left out
indicatorNotes.to change: the remaining letters change their order

blocks.note: the first letter of 'pleasure', dropped from SPARTAN
SPARTAN without its P
joins the fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An ascetic Spartan, avoiding pleasure, decides to transform into a high achiever.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'Spartan' meaning austere, which suits shunning pleasure. The question mark marks 'high flyer' as a pun on a high achiever.
annotation.definitionFit: Punning definition: a space traveller flies higher than anyone, so is literally a high flyer.

entries.clue: Food house husband leaves with unfinished letter (8)

indicatorNotes.leaves: the husband departs from the house
indicatorNotes.unfinished: the word stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: HOME = house, with H (husband) gone
LETTER minus its final R

annotation.surface: A house husband walks out, leaving an incomplete letter and some food behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House husband' reads as one role, a man who keeps house; split it, and h = husband is dropped from the word for house.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a dish of beaten eggs is one kind of food.

entries.clue: Strong point welcoming Greek characters — hint of future (9)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the strong point takes the characters inside it

blocks.note: a forte is someone's strong point
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: A fortress welcomes Greek visitors, a sign of things to come.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strong point' could be a fortified place, but it is a talent; 'characters' are letters, not people.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a small early sample of something still to come.

entries.clue: Boost man reportedly (6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as it is reported by word of mouth: heard, not read

blocks.note: a man's name, as heard; the spelling wanted is a different word

annotation.surface: A news item about promoting a man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a common way of asking for any man's name; here Philip, which sounds like a word for a stimulus.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a stimulus or lift, noun for noun.

entries.clue: Insect some classified as religious, almost blessed originally (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: the origin of each word, its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: some classified as religious, almost blessed
blocks.note: the first letter of each of these six words

annotation.surface: Some creatures are deemed sacred, nearly holy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer: the scarab beetle was sacred in ancient Egypt, so 'religious' and 'blessed' are true of it as well as supplying letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a dung beetle, which is an insect.

entries.clue: Drink valet uncovered (3)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: its covering, the first and last letters, is stripped away

blocks.note: VALET without V and T

annotation.surface: A manservant is caught drinking and exposed.
annotation.walkthrough: A valet is a gentleman's personal servant.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a kind of beer, and so a drink.

entries.clue: Provide protection for troubled sector (6)

indicatorNotes.troubled: the letters are disturbed out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Peacekeepers are sent to guard an unsettled district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Troubled sector' reads as a war zone, which is why the protection sits so naturally before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to accompany someone as a guard.

entries.clue: Portrait at right angles in print? (9)

annotation.definition: Portrait at right angles in print?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a painting of a person; in printing it is the upright page layout
turn that upright page through 90 degrees and it becomes the wide layout

annotation.surface: A painted portrait has been printed sideways.
annotation.walkthrough: Printers and word processors offer two page orientations, portrait and landscape; each is the other turned on its side.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: the wide page orientation is the tall one rotated by a right angle.

entries.clue: English editor displaying storage facility (4)

indicatorNotes.displaying: the words put the answer on show inside themselves

blocks.note: the letters run across the join: the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: A British editor shows off a warehouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'English editor' looks like two abbreviations, E and ED, but the answer sits whole across the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a garden hut used for keeping tools and the like.

entries.clue: Two needed for this tea, as communicated? (5)

blocks.note: a saying: it takes two to do this dance
the letter T, pronounced 'tea', as sent over the radio

annotation.surface: An invitation to tea for two, passed on by message.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It takes two to tango'; and in the NATO phonetic alphabet used over radio, T is sent as Tango.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom and a code word: the dance that takes two, and the radio call sign for T.

entries.clue: Crude translation of “get in lane” (9)

indicatorNotes.translation of: the words are rendered into a different form

blocks.note: anagram indicator
anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A road sign's instruction has been clumsily rendered into another language.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'get in lane' look like text to be translated, and it is: into a new order of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: lacking polish or refinement.

entries.clue: Regular temperature occurrence (5)

blocks.note: even = regular, steady
t = temperature

annotation.surface: A weather report notes that a steady temperature is normal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regular' seems to describe the occurrence, but it supplies the first piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something that happens.
